# HelpGetUp

> HelpGetUp (helpgetup.com) is a free guide for people stuck on food in Albany County, New York. It gives one clear next step: a pantry, community meal, produce stop, community fridge, or (for people 60+) a senior meal site open this week, or the official SNAP / EBT path (NYS myBenefits and the Albany County SNAP hotline). The person decides whether to take the step.

## Pages
- [Home and food walk](https://helpgetup.com/): pick "Hungry tonight", "SNAP / EBT", or "Both"; enter an Albany County ZIP or neighborhood; see stops with published hours this week, closest first. Spanish version: https://helpgetup.com/?lang=es (draft Spanish; place names and hours stay in English as published).
- [Full Albany County food list](https://helpgetup.com/albany-food-list): every listed place on one plain page, grouped by type, with address, phone, hours as published, eligibility notes, source, and check date. Best page to cite.
- [Lista completa en español (draft Spanish)](https://helpgetup.com/albany-food-list/es): the same list with Spanish headings, labels and help text. Place names, addresses, hours and notes stay in English as published. The Spanish is a draft awaiting native review.
- [Privacy](https://helpgetup.com/privacy): what the site and the Rosa talk button collect, Vercel Analytics, and how hello@helpgetup.com is used. The site sells nothing.

## Where the data comes from
- The Food Pantries for the Capital District's Food Connect map (https://map.thefoodpantries.org/) and its February 2026 Albany County resource flyer.
- Capital Roots' 2026 Veggie Mobile schedule (a low-cost produce market that takes EBT/SNAP; not free).
- Albany County Department for Aging congregate dining pages, plus LifePath, Colonie Senior Service Centers, and the Town of Berne for 60+ meal sites.
- Each place shows its source and the date the source was updated. Rows are re-checked against the sources; the page shows the list's last-checked date.

## What it does not do
- It does not call, fax, or send anything on a person's behalf, and it does not fill out government forms.
- It does not collect a Social Security number, driver's license, benefits password, or ID photo. The ZIP or neighborhood typed in stays in the browser.
- The home page has an optional signup (name and email) for updates and help resources. That is the only name and email the site asks for. See the privacy page.
- It is not an emergency service. In immediate danger, call 911.

## Scope and cautions
- Albany County, NY only. Food only (for now).
- Hours change. People should call the place, or the Food Pantries referral line (518) 458-1167, before going.

## Official sources it points to
- [NYS myBenefits](https://mybenefits.ny.gov/)
- [Albany County SNAP page](https://www.albanycountyny.gov/supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program-snap)
- [Food Connect map](https://map.thefoodpantries.org/)
